capabilities: Start and stop timers on checkbox tasks from commands, icons, or the status bar
Browse, search, and edit tracked sessions by day, week, or custom date range
Assign clients and projects to tasks and filter history by them
View a 30-day dashboard of time totals by project, client, day, and task
Export sessions as generic, Toggl-formatted, or Clockify-formatted CSV
extras: Explains limits in detail (identifier placement breaks Tasks queries, duplicated tt-ids, read-only views don't show controls). Warns about multi-device sync version mismatches that can lose client data. Harvest and Everhour export formats are planned. Nothing is ever transmitted externally; export files are written locally for manual upload.
motivation: The author built it because he needed it himself and couldn't find a plugin that did what he wanted.
problem: Obsidian has no native way to track time spent on tasks, and existing trackers focus on Pomodoro-style sessions or don't integrate with checkbox-based task formats.

relations.evidence: If you use the Tasks plugin, where the identifier sits on the line matters.
Dataview is entirely optional: tracking, history, and export all work exactly the same without it.
Toggl-formatted CSV — matches the exact columns expected by Toggl's official importer.
Clockify-formatted CSV — matches the exact columns expected by Clockify's Timesheets importer.

summary: Time tracker that records work sessions on checkbox tasks inside the vault and exports CSVs formatted for Toggl and Clockify importers.
